Now checking CI on the four PRs.","textTruncated":false,"nextTextOffset":null,"updatedAt":"2026-11-14T10:31:17.793Z"},{"position":155,"visibility":"local","sourceThreadId":"mcp:launch:ac446ed3c33ae8f448ec486f9439559322e8df7afe78d2656ec3b4875166841c","itemId":"turn-item:provider:claudeAgent:native-item:471281c8-fe4f-47bb-87cb-7b83eef12c46","runId":"run:thread:mcp%3Alaunch%3Aac446ed3c33ae8f448ec486f9439559322e8df7afe78d2656ec3b4875166841c:ordinal:2","messageId":"message:provider:claudeAgent:native-item:471281c8-fe4f-47bb-87cb-7b83eef12c46","createdBy":"agent","creationSource":"provider","type":"assistant_message","status":"completed","title":null,"text":"All four extractions are done and pushed as stacked PRs, each marked ready. `useMailbox.ts` went from 2,072 to 1,186 lines, with no changes to `App.vue`, `browsing-actions.ts`, `action-palette.ts`, `components/**`, `FixtureWorkspaces.vue` or `style.css`.

## PRs

| PR | Base | Head SHA | CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#50](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/50) selection | main | 9b9b33c | `check` passed on GitHub |
| [#51](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/51) groups | `maintenance/p5a-mailbox-selection` | 2d338c0 | none until retargeted to main |
| [#52](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/52) detail cache | `maintenance/p5a-mailbox-groups` | ce3d1cb | none until retargeted to main |
| [#53](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/53) account | `maintenance/p5a-mailbox-detail-cache` | 4adbbc5 | none until retargeted to main |

On each head I ran `mise run test:ui`, typecheck and `build:web`, and all passed. The rendered suite on #53's head is 33 of 34, failing only on the known large-text Inbox row test. I did not run cargo; CI covers the Rust suites. For #51–#53, checks only ran on #50 (the PR targeting main). I never saw them on the stacked PRs.

Every push landed (compared `rev-parse` against `ls-remote`). The pushes for #52 and #53 were rejected once and succeeded on an immediate retry.

## Tests and line counts

- **Test counts:** the baseline I confirmed on main is 1,454 in 84 files. After each PR: #50 1,459 in 85, #51 1,464 in 86, #52 1,473 in 87, #53 1,481 in 88. No test was deleted or weakened.
- **Baseline caveat:** my baseline run overlapped my first edits, but the counts match your 1,454 and everything passed.
- **Line counts:** `useMailbox.ts` is 1,186. The new modules are `useMailboxSelection` 175, `useMailboxGroups` 647, `useMailboxDetailCache` 141, `useMailboxAccount` 177, `mailbox-refs` 10 and `mailbox-session` 20.

## Non-move edits

Each PR description lists these in full:
- **Mechanical substitutions inside moved bodies:** `detached` becomes `session.detached` and `mailboxSessionToken` becomes `session.generation`. `commandToken` becomes `commands.next()`/`commands.current()`, and `++navigationIntentToken` becomes `supersedeNavigation()` in the account module. The remaining reads of parent state became small getter arguments.
- **New plain modules:** `mailbox-refs.ts` holds `sameConversation` and `copyRef`. `mailbox-session.ts` holds the `MailboxSession` (generation and detached flag) and `CommandFence` types.
- **New functions:** `afterAuthoritativeRefresh()` in groups wraps the four group calls that sat inline in `refresh()`. The detail cache gained two accessors, `currentDetailEpoch()` and `adoptablePrefetch()`, replacing direct reads in `loadDetail`. The account module gained `refreshAccountStatus()`, used at the two `refresh()` call sites.
- **Callback split in the account PR:** the account-change and post-disconnect reset blocks stay in `useMailbox` verbatim as `resetForAccountChange()` and `resetAfterDisconnect()`, and the account module calls them through callbacks.
- **Re-exports:** `useMailbox.ts` re-exports `SELECTION_MAX`, `sameConversation`, `GroupNotice`, `AccountState`, `AccountAction` and the three detail-cache constants.
- **Docs:** `docs/current-architecture.md` is updated in each PR.

## Stale-response proof per piece

- **Selection:** it has no async work, so the fence is explicit clearing. Existing proof is `useMailbox-safety.test.ts` "invalidates accepted saves immediately…". I added `useMailbox-selection.test.ts` "drops selection and anchor when the account identity changes or the account disconnects", plus 4 isolated unit tests.
- **Groups:**
  - Existing: `useMailbox-group-recovery.test.ts` "clears group surfaces on disconnect and rejects late old-session responses", "rejects old restart-notice discovery across a same-account reconnect" and "a stale pre-undo status response never overwrites…".
  - New: `useMailboxGroups.unit.test.ts` moves the session itself.
- **Detail cache:**
  - Existing: `navigation-smooth.test.ts` "drops an in-flight prefetch result after the reader closes".
  - New: "drops an in-flight prefetch… after an account change / disconnect", and `useMailboxDetailCache.unit.test.ts`.
  - Removing the epoch bump makes 5 of these fail.
- **Account:**
  - Existing: `useMailbox.test.ts` "guards stale status responses" and "disconnect clears the list and reader and drops stale in-flight responses".
  - New: `useMailboxAccount.unit.test.ts`.

## Needs a decision

- **Detail-cache fence:** it is its epoch, not the session generation. The owner calls `invalidateDetailCache()` on refresh, mutation start, reader close (which account change and disconnect both call) and dispose. The cache only receives `session.detached`. I did not add a generation check because it would change behaviour, but it is easy to add if you want it strictly generation-based.
- **Account PR:** `useMailbox` still owns the session counters, and the account module reaches them only through the two reset callbacks.
- **Frontend lint:** `mise.toml` has no frontend lint task, only Rust ones, so I ran none.

On each head I ran `mise run test:ui`, typecheck and `build:web`, and all passed. The rendered suite on #53's head is 33 of 34, failing only on the known large-text Inbox row test. I did not run cargo; CI covers the Rust suites. For #51–#53, checks only ran on #50 (the PR targeting main). I never saw them on the stacked PRs.

Every push landed (compared `rev-parse` against `ls-remote`). The pushes for #52 and #53 were rejected once and succeeded on an immediate retry.

## Tests and line counts

- **Test counts:** the baseline I confirmed on main is 1,454 in 84 files. After each PR: #50 1,459 in 85, #51 1,464 in 86, #52 1,473 in 87, #53 1,481 in 88. No test was deleted or weakened.
- **Baseline caveat:** my baseline run overlapped my first edits, but the counts match your 1,454 and everything passed.
- **Line counts:** `useMailbox.ts` is 1,186. The new modules are `useMailboxSelection` 175, `useMailboxGroups` 647, `useMailboxDetailCache` 141, `useMailboxAccount` 177, `mailbox-refs` 10 and `mailbox-session` 20.

## Non-move edits

Each PR description lists these in full:
- **Mechanical substitutions inside moved bodies:** `detached` becomes `session.detached` and `mailboxSessionToken` becomes `session.generation`. `commandToken` becomes `commands.next()`/`commands.current()`, and `++navigationIntentToken` becomes `supersedeNavigation()` in the account module. The remaining reads of parent state became small getter arguments.
- **New plain modules:** `mailbox-refs.ts` holds `sameConversation` and `copyRef`. `mailbox-session.ts` holds the `MailboxSession` (generation and detached flag) and `CommandFence` types.
- **New functions:** `afterAuthoritativeRefresh()` in groups wraps the four group calls that sat inline in `refresh()`. The detail cache gained two accessors, `currentDetailEpoch()` and `adoptablePrefetch()`, replacing direct reads in `loadDetail`. The account module gained `refreshAccountStatus()`, used at the two `refresh()` call sites.
- **Callback split in the account PR:** the account-change and post-disconnect reset blocks stay in `useMailbox` verbatim as `resetForAccountChange()` and `resetAfterDisconnect()`, and the account module calls them through callbacks.
- **Re-exports:** `useMailbox.ts` re-exports `SELECTION_MAX`, `sameConversation`, `GroupNotice`, `AccountState`, `AccountAction` and the three detail-cache constants.
- **Docs:** `docs/current-architecture.md` is updated in each PR.

## Stale-response proof per piece

- **Selection:** it has no async work, so the fence is explicit clearing. Existing proof is `useMailbox-safety.test.ts` "invalidates accepted saves immediately…". I added `useMailbox-selection.test.ts` "drops selection and anchor when the account identity changes or the account disconnects", plus 4 isolated unit tests.
- **Groups:**
  - Existing: `useMailbox-group-recovery.test.ts` "clears group surfaces on disconnect and rejects late old-session responses", "rejects old restart-notice discovery across a same-account reconnect" and "a stale pre-undo status response never overwrites…".
  - New: `useMailboxGroups.unit.test.ts` moves the session itself.
- **Detail cache:**
  - Existing: `navigation-smooth.test.ts` "drops an in-flight prefetch result after the reader closes".
  - New: "drops an in-flight prefetch… after an account change / disconnect", and `useMailboxDetailCache.unit.test.ts`.
  - Removing the epoch bump makes 5 of these fail.
- **Account:**
  - Existing: `useMailbox.test.ts` "guards stale status responses" and "disconnect clears the list and reader and drops stale in-flight responses".
  - New: `useMailboxAccount.unit.test.ts`.

## Needs a decision

- **Detail-cache fence:** it is its epoch, not the session generation. The owner calls `invalidateDetailCache()` on refresh, mutation start, reader close (which account change and disconnect both call) and dispose. The cache only receives `session.detached`. I did not add a generation check because it would change behaviour, but it is easy to add if you want it strictly generation-based.

## Design health score: 28/40 (Good, unchanged)

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | Cause and count are visible in the header. "Sign-in expired" sits beside "Idle · Never synced · 18 cached". |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 3 | "Offline" is gone. "no network" in the header vs "The network is unavailable" in the empty line and drawer. |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc cancels the disconnect confirm and returns focus. Cancel sign-in works. |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 2 | One action, four names: Connect Gmail, Connect, Sign in, Sign in again. Links in some places, chips in others. |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Two-step disconnect with a specific warning. The destructive button is a bare grey ghost with no danger cue. |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 3 | The first-run hint explains Connect, and the palette ranks it first. On failure Sync now is 9th. |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 3 | `g a` works. The drawer opens focus on the region, not the first control. |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 2 | The same fact appears twice in every zero-row state. |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry is one click and the cause is specific. Retry appears in three places when rows exist. |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 3 | The hint, permission disclosure and disconnect warning are good. "Starts read-only" is never explained. |
| **Total** | | **28/40** | |

The total did not move, but the failures changed. Four of the five issues from the last critique are fixed, and two new ones took their places in the scoring (header two-tab squeeze, wording duplication).

## Design specificity verdict
- **Design review (A):** authored for this product. The terse voice, the honest Status-Is-Sacred tinting and the careful disconnect flow could not belong to another app. The weak spot is the empty states: one sentence and a link on a blank 968px column, with an empty 272px contact column beside it.
- **Detector (B):** 0 findings in `AccountPanel`, `ProviderDestinations`, `ContactPane`, `ActionOverlay` and `App.vue`.
  - `FixtureWorkspaces.vue` does not exist at that path. The fixture code is `src/lib/fixture-workspaces.ts`, which also scanned clean.
  - `style.css` returned 6 findings, none in account code. Three `side-tab` hits are false positives (the deliberate 3–4px focus stripe on highlighted rows). Three `design-system-radius` hits (2px, 2px, 3px) are real but minor.
- **Overlay:** the injection succeeded, with no CSP block.
  - Disconnected and sync-error states: clean.
  - Sync-error with no rows: one real `straggler`. "available." sits alone on the second line of "No correspondent information is available." (`ContactPane.vue:137`).
  - Account drawer open: 12 `text-occlusion` hits, all false positives. The opaque drawer is meant to cover the list rows.

## Overall impression
The fixes landed, and several are better than they needed to be: the cause is in words, Connect is explained, and disconnect is trustworthy. What remains is repetition and the leftover header squeeze. The biggest opportunity is deciding which surface owns each fact, so the header and the empty line stop saying the same thing.

## What's working
1. **Disconnect flow.** The warning names exactly what is removed and kept, focus starts on "Keep account", and Esc returns it to "Disconnect…".
2. **Honest state vocabulary.** Pending, failed and unknown stay distinct, and the tint only echoes words. Contrast is 7.7 to 14.7:1.
3. **Discoverability.** Connect Gmail ranks first in the palette while disconnected, and `g a` is named in the rail title and the chord hint.

## Previous findings

| Finding | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 header squeeze at 1030px | **Partly fixed** | A single tab is fine (Inbox tab 62px, no clipping at 1280/1030/900). With a saved split, "Unread only" and the read-only hint, the Inbox tab is 13px wide and its label 0px wide. Only "18" shows. |
| P2 repeated actions | **Fixed for actions, not for wording** | The header link is dropped when the empty line carries the action. The sentence is still repeated. |
| P2 first-run clarity | **Partly fixed** | The hint line is there. "No correspondent information…" is gone when there is no account, but persists in auth-required, first sync, sync failure and connected-empty. |
| P2 cause and vocabulary | **Fixed** | "Sync failed · no network" is visible. "no network" vs "The network is unavailable" is a leftover. |
| P3 palette order | **Fixed** when disconnected, **partly** on failure | Sync now is 9th when sync fails. |
| P3 Keys rows | **Partly fixed** | One row, "Open destinations ←", remains when disconnected. |
| P3 sync facts labelled | **Fixed** | "Idle · Never synced · N conversations cached". |
| P3 Disconnect vs Keep account | **Fixed** | Keep account is filled with a focus ring. Disconnect now looks inert, though. |
| P3 duplicate "read only" | **Fixed** | The hint hides whenever a status note shows. |
| P3 coverage line | **Fixed** | Absent when disconnected. |

Regressions: none found.

## Priority issues

**[P1] The tab floor does not hold for two tabs plus Unread only at 1030px.**
- *Why it matters:* the active Inbox tab loses its label, which is the main navigation. "Unread only" ends at x=259 and the Preview tag starts at x=262, so they touch.
- *Fix:* compute the floor from tabs plus chip, collapse the read-only hint to its link text below about 1100px, or cap saved tab labels at about 12 characters.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable layout`

**[P2] The header note and the empty line duplicate each other in every zero-row state.**
- *Why it matters:* it is the same fact at 12px twice, 40px apart ("Not connected" / "Not connected."; a ticking "0 cached" shown twice during first sync). It undercuts the one-action-one-place rule.
- *Fix:* when the empty line carries the sentence, the header keeps only the Preview tag. Or the empty line carries only what the header can't: the hint and the action.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable distill`

**[P2] The first-run void is half addressed.**
- *Why it matters:* the right column is blank, and "No correspondent information is available." remains beside an empty list in four states (with a stray-word wrap). Jordan on `not_configured` gets a tiny "Account" link, then "connecting is unavailable" with no next step.
- *Fix:* hide the contact line when the list has no rows. Add one concrete line about what read-only means, or what happens on first sync. Give `not_configured` a next step.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable onboard`

items.text:
Method: dual-agent (A: `ad3094d18f153c6b6` · B: `a9c0019a493b27cd7`). Both were interrupted by a T3 server restart and resumed from their transcripts. They ran in isolated tabs against the rendered app at 1280, 1030 and 900px. The target is the account, connection and first-run UX at HEAD `3fbf1a7`. Compared against the 2026-11-09 snapshot (28/40).

## Design health score: 28/40 (Good, unchanged)

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | Cause and count are visible in the header. "Sign-in expired" sits beside "Idle · Never synced · 18 cached". |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 3 | "Offline" is gone. "no network" in the header vs "The network is unavailable" in the empty line and drawer. |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc cancels the disconnect confirm and returns focus. Cancel sign-in works. |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 2 | One action, four names: Connect Gmail, Connect, Sign in, Sign in again. Links in some places, chips in others. |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Two-step disconnect with a specific warning. The destructive button is a bare grey ghost with no danger cue. |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 3 | The first-run hint explains Connect, and the palette ranks it first. On failure Sync now is 9th. |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 3 | `g a` works. The drawer opens focus on the region, not the first control. |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 2 | The same fact appears twice in every zero-row state. |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry is one click and the cause is specific. Retry appears in three places when rows exist. |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 3 | The hint, permission disclosure and disconnect warning are good. "Starts read-only" is never explained. |
| **Total** | | **28/40** | |

The total did not move, but the failures changed. Four of the five issues from the last critique are fixed, and two new ones took their places in the scoring (header two-tab squeeze, wording duplication).

## Design specificity verdict
- **Design review (A):** authored for this product. The terse voice, the honest Status-Is-Sacred tinting and the careful disconnect flow could not belong to another app. The weak spot is the empty states: one sentence and a link on a blank 968px column, with an empty 272px contact column beside it.
- **Detector (B):** 0 findings in `AccountPanel`, `ProviderDestinations`, `ContactPane`, `ActionOverlay` and `App.vue`.
  - `FixtureWorkspaces.vue` does not exist at that path. The fixture code is `src/lib/fixture-workspaces.ts`, which also scanned clean.
  - `style.css` returned 6 findings, none in account code. Three `side-tab` hits are false positives (the deliberate 3–4px focus stripe on highlighted rows). Three `design-system-radius` hits (2px, 2px, 3px) are real but minor.
- **Overlay:** the injection succeeded, with no CSP block.
  - Disconnected and sync-error states: clean.
  - Sync-error with no rows: one real `straggler`. "available." sits alone on the second line of "No correspondent information is available." (`ContactPane.vue:137`).
  - Account drawer open: 12 `text-occlusion` hits, all false positives. The opaque drawer is meant to cover the list rows.

## Overall impression
The fixes landed, and several are better than they needed to be: the cause is in words, Connect is explained, and disconnect is trustworthy. What remains is repetition and the leftover header squeeze. The biggest opportunity is deciding which surface owns each fact, so the header and the empty line stop saying the same thing.

## What's working
1. **Disconnect flow.** The warning names exactly what is removed and kept, focus starts on "Keep account", and Esc returns it to "Disconnect…".
2. **Honest state vocabulary.** Pending, failed and unknown stay distinct, and the tint only echoes words. Contrast is 7.7 to 14.7:1.
3. **Discoverability.** Connect Gmail ranks first in the palette while disconnected, and `g a` is named in the rail title and the chord hint.

## Previous findings

| Finding | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 header squeeze at 1030px | **Partly fixed** | A single tab is fine (Inbox tab 62px, no clipping at 1280/1030/900). With a saved split, "Unread only" and the read-only hint, the Inbox tab is 13px wide and its label 0px wide. Only "18" shows. |
| P2 repeated actions | **Fixed for actions, not for wording** | The header link is dropped when the empty line carries the action. The sentence is still repeated. |
| P2 first-run clarity | **Partly fixed** | The hint line is there. "No correspondent information…" is gone when there is no account, but persists in auth-required, first sync, sync failure and connected-empty. |
| P2 cause and vocabulary | **Fixed** | "Sync failed · no network" is visible. "no network" vs "The network is unavailable" is a leftover. |
| P3 palette order | **Fixed** when disconnected, **partly** on failure | Sync now is 9th when sync fails. |
| P3 Keys rows | **Partly fixed** | One row, "Open destinations ←", remains when disconnected. |
| P3 sync facts labelled | **Fixed** | "Idle · Never synced · N conversations cached". |
| P3 Disconnect vs Keep account | **Fixed** | Keep account is filled with a focus ring. Disconnect now looks inert, though. |
| P3 duplicate "read only" | **Fixed** | The hint hides whenever a status note shows. |
| P3 coverage line | **Fixed** | Absent when disconnected. |

Regressions: none found.

## Priority issues

**[P1] The tab floor does not hold for two tabs plus Unread only at 1030px.**
- *Why it matters:* the active Inbox tab loses its label, which is the main navigation. "Unread only" ends at x=259 and the Preview tag starts at x=262, so they touch.
- *Fix:* compute the floor from tabs plus chip, collapse the read-only hint to its link text below about 1100px, or cap saved tab labels at about 12 characters.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable layout`

**[P2] The header note and the empty line duplicate each other in every zero-row state.**
- *Why it matters:* it is the same fact at 12px twice, 40px apart ("Not connected" / "Not connected."; a ticking "0 cached" shown twice during first sync). It undercuts the one-action-one-place rule.
- *Fix:* when the empty line carries the sentence, the header keeps only the Preview tag. Or the empty line carries only what the header can't: the hint and the action.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable distill`

**[P2] The first-run void is half addressed.**
- *Why it matters:* the right column is blank, and "No correspondent information is available." remains beside an empty list in four states (with a stray-word wrap). Jordan on `not_configured` gets a tiny "Account" link, then "connecting is unavailable" with no next step.
- *Fix:* hide the contact line when the list has no rows. Add one concrete line about what read-only means, or what happens on first sync. Give `not_configured` a next step.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable onboard`

**[P3] Names and tone are inc

I did not re-measure the header in a browser, so the header fix is unconfirmed at 1030px. I haven't re-run the critique either, so I can't say yet whether the 28/40 score moves.

The subagent hit your usage limit partway through, so I ran the checks and did the commit and push myself. Its changes were already in the worktree.

- **Header tab floor:** the tab column now has a minimum width worked out from the tab strip, so two tabs plus "Unread only" no longer crush the Inbox label. A saved-tab label stops at 12 characters with an ellipsis. At 1100px and below, the read-only hint shrinks to its "Review access" link.
- **One owner for status:** when the empty inbox line shows the status, the header note keeps only a hidden announcement and the Preview tag stays. The ticking cached count no longer shows twice.
- **First-run void:**
  - The contact pane says nothing when the list has no rows, and `text-wrap: balance` is set to stop the one-word wrap.
  - A device where Gmail isn't configured gets a next step in the empty line and the drawer ("Add a Google client ID to the launch environment, then restart"). The "connecting is unavailable" wording is gone.
  - The Connect line now says what read-only means.
- **Names and tone:** every surface uses Connect Gmail, Sign in again, Cancel sign-in, Retry and Sync now. The network cause reads "no network" everywhere. The Disconnect confirm has a coral text and border cue, and Keep account stays focused.
- **Drawer facts and announcements:**
  - The mode row and Sync section are hidden while disconnected, not configured or signing in.
  - A sync failure shows one coral line with Retry, and "Sign-in expired" appears once.
  - The header note stays silent while the drawer shows the same failure.
  - Sync now leads the palette on a sync failure.

I deferred or left alone:
- **Drawer focus on open:** it stays on the region, because that is the shared pattern for every drawer.
- **"Open destinations ←" row:** it stays in the palette with no account, because Left still opens the navigator.
- **Hit area and icon contrast:** I did not touch the 36×16 Retry hit area or the 4.30:1 rail icon contrast.

Still unverified: layout at real widths, `text-wrap: balance` rendering, real Google sign-in, the macOS Keychain, native offline behaviour, screen-reader output and Tab order in the drawer.

- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable polish`

- *Why it matters:* the empty line says "Add a Google client ID…", while the palette (`App.vue:1716`) and the drawer (`AccountPanel.vue:99`) still offer Connect Gmail. In the harness, running it flipped the inbox. This is the pre-existing behaviour I flagged as unchanged and deferred last pass, and the new line makes the contradiction visible.
- *Fix:* drop `not_configured` from both and let the drawer show the next-step line instead.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable clarify`

**[P2] At 1030px the squeeze moved from the tabs to the status.**
- *Why it matters:* with two tabs, "Unread only" and a sync failure, the note clips to about 36 of 145px of words ("Syn…") and the Preview tag clips to 88 of 124px. In the connected case, "Review access" clips by about 11px at 1030px. The failure is the fact most worth reading.
- *Fix:* let the Preview tag yield first, or have the cause yield before "Sync failed".
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable adapt`

**[P3] Visible duplicate Retry while the drawer is open.**
- *Why it matters:* announcements are fixed, but the header "Retry" and the drawer "Retry" are both visible.
- *Fix:* hide the header link while the drawer shows the failure.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable distill`

**[P3] Empty chrome.**
- *Why it matters:* the blank 272px contact column at 1280px, and a rail Contact drawer holding only "Contact" and "Close" at 900px.
- *Fix:* collapse the pane and remove the rail button when there are no rows.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable layout`

- **Jordan (first-timer).** "Account" is a bare link, the one required step is a 16px target, and "Never synced · 18 cached" and "Provider snapshots" are ja

- **Connect when not configured:** the palette no longer lists "Connect Gmail" and the drawer no longer shows a Connect button. The drawer shows the next-step note instead. Disconnected still offers "Connect Gmail" and expired still offers "Sign in again". I retargeted the tests that clicked Connect on a not-configured device, so they now assert the note and no button.
- **1030px header:** the agent measured this in headless Chromium against the in-memory fake.

- PR #34 head is c191432. Read docs/development.md and docs/current-architecture.md on main for the current test layout and commands.

STEP 1: bring the branch up to date
- `git fetch origin` and merge origin/main into `impeccable/account-first-run` (merge, not rebase, so the PR history stays reviewable). Resolve every conflict so that main's behaviour and this PR's design changes both survive. Where the two genuinely disagree (for example main reworked a surface you also changed), keep main's structure and re-apply your change on top, and note it for the report.
- Tests: follow main's conventions. Put this PR's new test files in the matching feature folder, use the shared helpers and fake timers instead of local copies, and do not reintroduce helpers main removed. Every test that exists on main must still be present and pass. If one of your deliberate UI changes requires changing an assertion in a main test, list each such change with the reason. No test is deleted or weakened without naming its replacement.
- Fetch again before final validation and merge main once more if it moved (the remaining `useMailbox` split PRs will land; they do not touch your files).

STEP 2: validate
- Machine: 2 CPU cores, 7 GB RAM, about 4 GB free disk, shared with one other thread running cargo. One heavy command at a time, including across subagents. Export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target before any mise/cargo command and never hardcode a target dir.
- Run `mise run install:ui`, then `mise run check:all`. Baseline on main after the split lands: frontend 1,481 tests in 88 files, mail-core 327, email-os 14. Report your counts.
- Run the rendered suite once on the final head: `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome mise run test:rendered`. Baseline on main is 33 of 34; the one failure is the known large-text Inbox row overflow (`tests/browsing/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts`, "collapses overflowing row actions…"). Do not fix or touch that test in this PR. Any other rendered failure is yours to fix. If your header/tab-floor and contact-pane layout rules can be pinned by a rendered test in that suite, add one or two; that replaces the one-off browser measurements with something repeatable.
- Push, confirm the push landed (`git rev-parse HEAD` vs `git ls-remote origin impeccable/account-first-run`), and check that PR #34 shows as mergeable with CI `check` green. The git remote is a proxy URL, so `gh` needs `-R BbrSofiane/email-os`.

STEP 3: one closing critique
- Run `/impeccable critique` once on the merged head, the same way as before (rendered at 900, 1030 and 1280px), against the 29.5/40 baseline.
- Exit rule, so this converges: fix every P0 or P1 and every regression it finds. Fix P2 items only if each is small and local, in one pass. Then stop. Do not start another critique-and-fix round. Put the remaining P2/P3 items in the PR description as follow-ups.
- After any fix, re-run step 2's checks on the final head.

BOUNDARIES
- Stay within this PR's existing scope. Do not edit `src/composables/useMailbox*.ts`, `src/composables/mailbox-*.ts` or `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts` beyond what a conflict resolution strictly requires (another thread is working on the fake's contract tests). No Rust changes.
- Synthetic fixtures only; no real accounts, credentials or Google network. Do not edit the root checkout /home/exedev/email-os.
- If you hit a product decision, or a conflict where you cannot keep both sides' intent, stop and report it with the evidence rather than choosing silently.

FINAL REPORT (your last message)
Head SHA and CI state; test counts (frontend, core, native, rendered); every conflict resolution that needed judgment; every main test whose assertions you changed and why; the critique score and what you fixed after it; remaining follow-ups; and what is still unverified.

items.text:
You are one implementation thread in a coordinated maintenance programme for Email OS, following a code review. A coordinating thread (not you) sequences tickets, reviews and merges PRs, and runs end-to-end validation. This is implementation, not another review.

HOW TO WORK
- The user chose Claude Sonnet 5.5 for these threads. Where work splits cleanly into non-overlapping files, use your native
I'll start with the repo instructions and docs, then do the rename.
The ticket missed something: `gmail/provider.rs:76` already defines a concrete `pub struct GmailProvider`, the live HTTP implementation. I'll gather the evidence before deciding.

I've messaged the coordinator about the `GmailProvider` name collision blocking PR A, and I'm now starting PR B since it doesn't depend on that name. Next I'm reading the test support and the existing undo and group rules.
Still reading: I'm going through how the browser fake implements operations, undo and groups. That tells me what the scenario format has to cover.
You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 5:30am (UTC)
Continue where you left off.

PR A is blocked on the coordinator's answer about the name collision, and I'm done reading the fake and DTOs on PR B. Next I'm checking the Rust test-support API for the scenario format's provider-outcome vocabulary.

Coordinator decision on the T11 name collision: take your option 1. The trait `gmail::types::GmailReadProvider` becomes `GmailProvider`, and the concrete struct `gmail::provider::GmailProvider` becomes `LiveGmailProvider`. Two public names change instead of one; that is approved, and say so in the PR description. Do it as two commits (struct rename first, then trait rename) so each is reviewable,
Coordinator approved option 1. I'm switching to the PR A branch now to do the two-commit rename, struct first and then trait.
Status: both rename commits are pushed. I'm opening the draft PR and running `mise run check:all` on it.
PR A is sent and PR B's scenario format is designed. I'm now checking how the native shell rejects unsupported commands on the fixture backend, since the Rust runner has to match it.
Status: draft PR #55 is open with the Rust runner and the first scenario passing on both backends. Now I'm writing the rest of the scenarios.

32 of 33 scenario runs pass on both Rust backends, but a failed group member on Gmail leaves its queued sibling pending, so I'm reading the worker code to tell a scenario artifact from a real backend difference.
Status: the new read/star/retry and fixture-only scenarios pass on the Rust backends apart from star undo. I'm checking what the star undo rule actually is in UX-08.
Status: I'm adding a small optional mailbox-seed hook to the browser fake so scenario mailboxes can be loaded, then writing the Vitest runner.
Good, `vite/client` types are available, so `import.meta.glob` works. Writing the shared TS helper and the runner test.
Status: I'm fixing the remaining small fake divergences the scenarios exposed: group-undo eligibility, request-id validation, and the serial worker.
Status: the fake fixes are narrowed to three known-divergence entries plus uncontroversial fixes. Two existing fake tests still fail because of the serial-worker change, so I'm looking at them.
Status: writing the docs now, a "Contract scenarios" section in `docs/development.md` and the parity guarantee in `docs/current-architecture.md`.
Status: the fake-side and Rust Gmail mutations all fail as expected. The fixture-store supersession mutation didn't apply because of an off-by-one line, so I'm redoing it.
Status: everything is validated and pushed, so I'm filling in the PR B description and marking it ready.

PR B is ready for review and CI is running; a CI result will wake me. The CI row below is therefore partly open.

content.thinking:
I've finished the T17 pass and found three known divergences that need decisions. The first is KD-1: after a definite provider failure, the Gmail worker enters sync-error backoff and leaves its queued siblings queued, while the fixture worker and the fake keep draining. That also seems to mean every Rust run waits out the 5-second bound, which would be real waiting in the scenario test, and I said I'd never do that, so I need to look at it.

I'm weighing whether the Gmail worker's backoff after a definite provider failure is intended behavior or a bug. Since the fixture will run on GmailCore after the unification step, the Gmail semantics should win, so the fake should match them, with queued siblings staying queued until the next pass.

I'm looking at the two remaining divergences. KD-2 is the fixture's `setRead` error, where the shell says `invalid_request` and the fake says `read_only`, which is the inconsistency I already spotted in my original review and should disappear once the fixture gains read and star. For KD-3, the Rust core accepts an undo of an all-ineligible group and marks every member skipped, while the fake rejects it with `not_applicable`; I'm leaning toward making the fake match Rust and updating the existing test, though I still need to check whether the UI tests depend on the fake's current behaviour.

I'm checking whether the 5-second bound in the KD-1 scenario means real waiting in every Rust run, since that would break my rule against real waiting in tests. Before deciding anything about the worker's backoff, I want to look at the PR #55 diff stat and how the fake's serial draining changed, to see whether the UI tests that run against the fake still hold up.

Any error during a mutation pass seems to stop the remaining queued operations until the next sync tick, with the delay growing through backoff. That fits a network-unavailable error, but a definite per-operation failure like a 404 or 400 probably shouldn't hold up the sibling operations. I'm wondering what happens in that case.

I'm checking how run_one maps a definite provider failure to an error, since that decides whether siblings stall. This looks like a deliberate safety choice in Gmail mode rather than a bug, so I'll flag it to the user with a recommendation and leave the code alone. For parity, KD-1 stays as a named divergence, and KD-3 could be fixed either now in #55 or as a follow-up in T14's first PR to avoid re-gating.

I'm planning the next steps: once #55 merges, I'll launch the T14 thread, since it needs those scenarios as its parity net, and the gate takes about 11 minutes. Meanwhile I'll prepare the T14 brief. For ADR #45, I'm considering merging it as-is with status "Proposed" and having T14's first PR move it to "Accepted" with the decisions recorded.

I'm settling on the ADR: I'll mark it Accepted, noting that it's on the coordinator's recommendation and the user asked for the remaining tickets to run, and that the decisions can be revisited before stage 4. The first decision is staged unification rather than a fallback, and the second is that the fixture gains read and star at stage 4 through an explicit session policy.

I'm settling the remaining ADR decisions: the second one is that the fixture gains read and star at stage 4, which means relaxing a restriction rather than adding code to block those actions. I'm also noting the mutation-access distinction, with the fixture reporting it as granted, and that reminders and the one-time on-disk reset with a retained backup follow the same pattern.

I'm weighing whether the fixture should gain read and star, since that would change what the UI shows in fixture mode, which the UI tests and browser preview both run in. I'm checking whether the frontend currently hides those actions there, because if they're hidden now, enabling them means the capability gating and the related tests would all need to change together.

Next I'm planning the T14 brief around the ADR 0002 stages, with a hard checkpoint after stage 3 where the thread has to inventory the UI impact before switching fixture mode to read and star. Since fixture mode is what the UI tests and browser preview run in, that switch could change a lot of expectations, so I want the user to weigh in before it happens. T16 comes after T14, since the thin-shell split is easier once the fixture work has landed.

I'm putting together the brief for the T14 thread now: it'll follow the ADR 0002 stages, with one PR per stage. Stage 1 ports the fixture guarantee tests to GmailCore and adds the synthetic provider module while leaving the default fixture path untouched. Stage 2 adds the session policy and persistent synthetic facts, and stage 3 brings in reminders and attachment seams behind an opt-in env var, with a stop-and-report checkpoint before the stage 4 switch.

I'm settling the rest of the plan for the T14 brief: it runs in stages from the ADR, with a stop-and-report checkpoint before the stage 4 switch, since that's the first point where fixture behaviour changes. I also want Gmail mode to stay identical at every stage, with the existing Gmail tests unchanged, and I'll add a third "synthetic" profile to the contract scenarios as parity evidence. content.text:
The `useMailbox` split is fully merged (#50 to #53, ticket 19 done), and the shared contract scenarios (ticket 17, #55) are finished and in my gate now. Main is at `def0950`, which also includes the ADR from #45 (docs only, still marked Proposed).

**Contract scenarios (#55)**
- 26 scenario files run against the Gmail core, the fixture core and the browser fake: 45 runs on each side.
- The thread proved the net works by breaking a rule on each side in turn (undo window, supersession) and watching the matching runner fail.
- The scenarios exposed four places where the browser fake disagreed with the Rust core; all four are fixed in the PR: activity ordering, a serial worker, group replay identity, and request-id validation.

**Three disagreements it found and left visible** (each is a named entry that must keep failing until resolved):
1. **Gmail worker stalls siblings after a failure.** When one operation fails definitively, the Gmail worker ends its pass and backs off, so other queued operations stay queued until the next tick. The fixture worker and the fake keep going. This affects real Gmail use: one failed member of a group archive delays the rest. I have not changed it; say if you want the worker to keep draining.
2. **Fixture `setRead` error type.** The native shell answers `invalid_request`, the fake answers `read_only`. This disappears when fixture mode gains read and star in ticket 14.
3. **Undo on a group with no eligible member.** Both Rust stores accept it and mark every member skipped; the fake rejects it. I'll have the fake aligned to the Rust behaviour during ticket 14.

**Next**
- Merge #55 if the gate passes, then launch the fixture unification thread (ticket 14) on Sonnet 5.5. It will stop and report after stage 3, before anything changes default fixture behaviour.
- The PR #34 thread is working through its merge with main.

When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
