input.title: Gmail worker: keep draining after a rejected write
input.message:
You are fixing a known divergence in the Email OS Gmail worker (called KD-1 in the repo). I coordinate the maintenance programme from thread `c07c9c54-0efc-4c81-81d7-dc1548e15e3c`; I run the full end-to-end gate and merge. You open the PR and do not merge.

## The problem
When Gmail definitely rejects one queued mailbox write, the worker ends its pass in sync-error backoff, so the other queued writes (for example the other members of a group archive) stay `queued` until the next retry tick: about a minute, and up to 10 minutes after repeated failures (`MAX_BACKOFF_INTERVAL` in `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs`). The browser fake drains them immediately. The owner has decided: **the worker should keep draining past a write that was definitely rejected, and keep backing off when the account or the network is the problem.**

## Where it is
- `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs`, `run_one`. It already separates the cases:
  - transient or account-wide errors (`NetworkUnavailable`, `ProviderUnavailable`, `InvalidProviderResponse`, `RateLimited`, `AuthRequired`, `PermissionRequired`, `SecretsUnavailable`) requeue the operation and return `Err`. **Keep this: stop and back off.**
  - the catch-all arm calls `store.fail_operation` and then also returns `Err`. This is the definite, operation-scoped rejection. **This is the one to change**, so the pass continues to the next queued write.
  - `StorageUnavailable` halts. Keep.
  - the account-mismatch branch (`profile.account_id != record.account_id`) is account-wide. Keep it stopping.
- `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs` around the `PassAction::Mutations` branch turns `run_one`'s result into `PassOutcome::{Complete, Idle, SyncError, Halt, Cancelled}`.
- `crates/mail-core/tests/contract_scenarios.rs`: `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` has two KD-1 entries (profiles `gmail` and `synthetic`) for scenario `group-member-failure-does-not-stop-siblings`. The runner requires listed scenarios to fail, so both entries must go once this works.
- `sync.rs` test `synthetic_tick_rearms_queued_writes_after_a_definite_failure` asserts the old behaviour (sibling stays `Queued` until the tick).

## What I need you to decide and show
Read the code before choosing the shape of the change. I think the smallest correct change is for the definite-rejection arm to finish as a completed pass, but check these and say what you found:
1. What does the user lose if that failure no longer becomes a `SyncError`? The failed operation must still show as failed with its error and stay retryable from Activity. If the account status line currently relies on the `SyncError` to tell the user anything they would otherwise miss, say so and keep that information reachable.
2. Backoff state: a completed pass resets `st.backoff`. Is it right that a definite rejection, which proves the provider answered, clears backoff built up by earlier transient failures? Decide and justify in the PR.
3. Uncertain-outcome reconciliation (`reconcile`, `finish_unlanded`) has its own failure paths. Do not change them unless the same stall exists there; if it does, report it instead of widening this PR.
4. Which errors actually reach the catch-all arm today? List them in the PR so the owner can see nothing account-wide is hiding there. If one of them is really account-wide, move it to the stop-and-back-off arm.

## Tests (write the failing ones first)
- Definite rejection of the first of two queued writes: the second is `Confirmed` without any tick, for both the `gmail` and `synthetic` profiles.
- Transient failure of the first: the second stays `Queued` and the pass ends in backoff (the behaviour that must not change).
- The review finding behind `synthetic_tick_rearms_queued_writes_after_a_definite_failure` was "with discovery off, the periodic tick must still re-arm queued writes". That property still matters after a transient failure. Keep a test for it, driven by a transient failure, if the synthetic provider or the shared fake can inject one; if neither can, say so rather than dropping the coverage silently.
- Remove both `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` entries; the contract scenario must now pass on both Rust profiles.

## Docs
Update what describes KD-1 as current behaviour: `docs/development.md` (the "today only KD-1" sentence), `docs/current-architecture.md` if it names it, and any other mention you find by searching for `KD-1` and "definite failure".

## Tell the owner the cost
In the PR description, state plainly: if Gmail rejects every write, the queue now fails one by one without pausing; each failed write stays retryable from Activity.

## Rules
- Share the cargo target: `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target`. Run one heavy command at a time. The shared target can serve stale results from other checkouts: `touch crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs src-tauri/src/lib.rs src-tauri/src/main.rs` before lint, and `touch crates/mail-core/src/bin/generate-types.rs crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs` before `mise run check:contract`.
- Before the PR: `mise run check:all` green. Report test counts (main today: mail-core 366, native 18, frontend 1,888 in 104 files).
- No wire-contract change is expected. If `check:contract` shows a diff after the touch above, stop and tell me.
- Privacy rule: never log subjects, addresses, bodies, tokens, URLs with ids, or SQL with bound values.
- Synthetic fixtures only. No real accounts, credentials or Google network.
- Never touch the root checkout `/home/exedev/email-os` except `git fetch`. Work in your worktree.
- PR to `main` on `BbrSofiane/email-os` (the remote is a proxy URL: pass `-R BbrSofiane/email-os` to `gh`). Commit at checkpoints so nothing is lost if you are cut off.

## Report
End with: the shape you chose and why, answers to the four questions above, tests added or changed, test counts, anything not verified, and the PR URL.

input.title: Gmail worker: keep draining after a rejected write
input.message:
You are fixing a known divergence in the Email OS Gmail worker (called KD-1 in the repo). I coordinate the maintenance programme from thread `c07c9c54-0efc-4c81-81d7-dc1548e15e3c`; I run the full end-to-end gate and merge. You open the PR and do not merge.

## The problem
When Gmail definitely rejects one queued mailbox write, the worker ends its pass in sync-error backoff, so the other queued writes (for example the other members of a group archive) stay `queued` until the next retry tick: about a minute, and up to 10 minutes after repeated failures (`MAX_BACKOFF_INTERVAL` in `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs`). The browser fake drains them immediately. The owner has decided: **the worker should keep draining past a write that was definitely rejected, and keep backing off when the account or the network is the problem.**

## Where it is
- `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs`, `run_one`. It already separates the cases:
  - transient or account-wide errors (`NetworkUnavailable`, `ProviderUnavailable`, `InvalidProviderResponse`, `RateLimited`, `AuthRequired`, `PermissionRequired`, `SecretsUnavailable`) requeue the operation and return `Err`. **Keep this: stop and back off.**
  - the catch-all arm calls `store.fail_operation` and then also returns `Err`. This is the definite, operation-scoped rejection. **This is the one to change**, so the pass continues to the next queued write.
  - `StorageUnavailable` halts. Keep.
  - the account-mismatch branch (`profile.account_id != record.account_id`) is account-wide. Keep it stopping.
- `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs` around the `PassAction::Mutations` branch turns `run_one`'s result into `PassOutcome::{Complete, Idle, SyncError, Halt, Cancelled}`.
- `crates/mail-core/tests/contract_scenarios.rs`: `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` has two KD-1 entries (profiles `gmail` and `synthetic`) for scenario `group-member-failure-does-not-stop-siblings`. The runner requires listed scenarios to fail, so both entries must go once this works.
- `sync.rs` test `synthetic_tick_rearms_queued_writes_after_a_definite_failure` asserts the old behaviour (sibling stays `Queued` until the tick).

## What I need you to decide and show
Read the code before choosing the shape of the change. I think the smallest correct change is for the definite-rejection arm to finish as a completed pass, but check these and say what you found:
1. What does the user lose if that failure no longer becomes a `SyncError`? The failed operation must still show as failed with its error and stay retryable from Activity. If the account status line currently relies on the `SyncError` to tell the user anything they would otherwise miss, say so and keep that information reachable.
2. Backoff state: a completed pass resets `st.backoff`. Is it right that a definite rejection, which proves the provider answered, clears backoff built up by earlier transient failures? Decide and justify in the PR.
3. Uncertain-outcome reconciliation (`reconcile`, `finish_unlanded`) has its own failure paths. Do not change them unless the same stall exists there; if it does, report it instead of widening this PR.
4. Which errors actually reach the catch-all arm today? List them in the PR so the owner can see nothing account-wide is hiding there. If one of them is really account-wide, move it to the stop-and-back-off arm.

## Tests (write the failing ones first)
- Definite rejection of the first of two queued writes: the second is `Confirmed` without any tick, for both the `gmail` and `synthetic` profiles.
- Transient failure of the first: the second stays `Queued` and the pass ends in backoff (the behaviour that must not change).
- The review finding behind `synthetic_tick_rearms_queued_writes_after_a_definite_failure` was "with discovery off, the periodic tick must still re-arm queued writes". That property still matters after a transient failure. Keep a test for it, driven by a transient failure, if the synthetic provider or the shared fake can inject one; if neither can, say so rather than dropping the coverage silently.
- Remove both `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` entries; the contract scenario must now pass on both Rust profiles.

## Docs
Update what describes KD-1 as current behaviour: `docs/development.md` (the "today only KD-1" sentence), `docs/current-architecture.md` if it names it, and any other mention you find by searching for `KD-1` and "definite failure".

## Tell the owner the cost
In the PR description, state plainly: if Gmail rejects every write, the queue now fails one by one without pausing; each failed write stays retryable from Activity.

## Rules
- Share the cargo target: `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target`. Run one heavy command at a time. The shared target can serve stale results from other checkouts: `touch crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs src-tauri/src/lib.rs src-tauri/src/main.rs` before lint, and `touch crates/mail-core/src/bin/generate-types.rs crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs` before `mise run check:contract`.
- Before the PR: `mise run check:all` green. Report test counts (main today: mail-core 366, native 18, frontend 1,888 in 104 files).
- No wire-contract change is expected. If `check:contract` shows a diff after the touch above, stop and tell me.
- Privacy rule: never log subjects, addresses, bodies, tokens, URLs with ids, or SQL with bound values.
- Synthetic fixtures only. No real accounts, credentials or Google network.
- Never touch the root checkout `/home/exedev/email-os` except `git fetch`. Work in your worktree.
- PR to `main` on `BbrSofiane/email-os` (the remote is a proxy URL: pass `-R BbrSofiane/email-os` to `gh`). Commit at checkpoints so nothing is lost if you are cut off.

## Report
End with: the shape you chose and why, answers to the four questions above, tests added or changed, test counts, anything not verified, and the PR URL.

## PR 1: minimum window width so 200% text cannot overflow the Inbox row
Branch `maintenance/followups-min-width` (your worktree's branch), base `main`.

**Background.** PR #57's description has the measurements (read it: `gh pr view 57 -R BbrSofiane/email-os`). In the worst-case row (old date, unknown read state, held unarchive) the compact Inbox row fits up to a 30.25px root font at 1000px wide and up to 36.5px at 1100px. So 32px text (200%) overflows by 27px at 1000px. The window opens at 1100px (`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`) and has no minimum width. The owner chose: keep the row as it is and add a minimum window width, rather than tighten the documented 12px gaps or lower the sender/subject floors.

**Do.**
1. Measure, in the rendered harness (`tests/browsing/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts`, real Chrome), the smallest width at which the worst-case compact row has zero overflow at a 32px root font. My interpolation says about 1030px; treat that as a guess.
2. Set `minWidth` on the main window in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` to that width plus a margin, rounded to a tidy number. The native webview is WebKit, not Chrome, and nobody has measured it there, so the margin is the allowance for that: state the measured bound and the margin you chose. Do not exceed the 1100px default width.
3. Add a rendered test step that reads `minWidth` from `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` and asserts the worst-case row does not overflow at that width with a 32px root font, so the config and the layout cannot drift apart. It must fail if `minWidth` is lowered to 1000.
4. Record the decision in `DESIGN.md` beside the existing large-text checkpoints ("Type scale and dates").
5. Check whether a minimum height is already implied anywhere; do not add one unless a test needs it. Do not change any CSS in this PR.

In the PR description say what is not covered: tiling window managers may ignore a minimum size, Android is unaffected, WebKit is unmeasured.

Branch `maintenance/followups-account-ui`, base `main` (independent of PR 1).

PR #34's description ends with a list of deferred follow-ups (`gh pr view 34 -R BbrSofiane/email-os`). - g-chord hint advertising keys that do nothing while disconnected (for example `g e`).
- Palette offering Create split and Show unread only on an Inbox with zero rows.
- Provider mail not saying so when the sign-in has expired.
- The duplicate empty `action-notice` live region.
- Inline action hit areas that are 16px high. Use the minimum target the project's `DESIGN.md` sets; if it sets none, use 24px and say so. Enlarge the hit area, not the glyph or the row height, and prove it with a rendered measurement.

**Re-check and report, fix only if it is a real bug on main:**
- "Fixture inconsistencies (rows=0 still `18 conversations cached`)". Unification may have removed it. Say what you found.

**Close without change (list them in the PR description as "not done, by the owner's decision"):**
- Palette name `Sync now` vs `Retry`.
- `Disconnect…` 8px indent.
- `connect` keyword on Go to Account when not configured.
- Under 1100px, `Mailbox permission pending` / `Gmail is read-only` collapsing to a bare `Review access` (PR 1's minimum width mostly removes the case).

Availability rules belong in the registry or the existing availability functions, not in new `if`s in `App.vue`. Copy changes follow the wording already in `src/lib/account-status.ts`.

## PR 3: two more extractions from App.vue (ticket 20, continued)
Branch `maintenance/followups-app-shell`, stacked on PR 2's branch if PR 2 touches `src/App.vue`, otherwise on `main`. Say which.

Earlier extractions (#60) moved `useGoChord`, `useActionNotice`, `useAccountNotes`, `useContactContext`, `useSearchSurface` and `src/lib/error-text.ts` out. Do the next two, in this order, as separate commits:
1. Viewport and contact-disclosure handling.
2. Attachment chooser state.

Rules for this PR:
- Pure moves. No behaviour change, no renamed user-facing strings, no test expectation changes. If a test needs changing, stop and tell me why.
- **Do not touch reader navigation or focus restoration.** That is where the Undo focus race was fixed (#62) and its timing is thinly tested. If either extraction cannot be done without reaching into it, do the part that can and report the rest.
- I verify moves by comparing whitespace-normalised line multisets per commit, so keep moved code textually the same and put any unavoidable glue (imports, the composable's return object, call sites) in as few lines as possible.
- The 1,800-line target is retired by the owner's decision. Report the new line count; do not chase a number. If any doc states the 1,800 target as current, update it to say the target was retired and why (the remaining bulk is reader navigation and focus, left alone deliberately).

Rendered tests time out when the machine is loaded: if you see timeouts, check `uptime` and rerun once it is quiet before believing them.
- New tests must fail against the unchanged code first. Say that you checked.

- Never touch the root checkout `/home/exedev/email-os` except `git fetch`. Create your further branches as worktrees or by switching branches inside your own worktree.

thread.title: Android smoke on the unified fixture

items.text:
You are running the Android device smoke for Email OS on current main (`3061e54`). I coordinate the maintenance programme from thread `c07c9c54-0efc-4c81-81d7-dc1548e15e3c`; I review and merge, you do not merge.

## Why
The Android fixture APK was last smoke-tested on an emulator on 14 Nov, before fixture mode moved onto the unified core (`GmailCore` + built-in synthetic provider, ADR 0002) and before the native shell was split (#68, #69). `docs/current-status.md` says so itself ("before the unified fixture became the default: re-run the smoke"). CI builds the APK, but nobody has run today's APK on a device, and the one-time legacy-fixture reset screen has never been seen on Android. The owner asked for this to be run.

## What to do
1. **Device.** An Android 15 emulator is already booted on this machine: hostId `local`, device id `emulator-5554` (name `t3-pixel`). Load the device tools with ToolSearch `select:mcp__t3-code__device_list,mcp__t3-code__device_open,mcp__t3-code__device_screenshot,mcp__t3-code__device_close`, call `device_open` with that hostId and id, and use the `agent-device` command it returns for every launch, tap, text entry and screenshot. `adb` is fine for installs, file copies, `run-as` and logs only. Do not drive the UI with raw `adb shell input`.
2. **APKs, from CI (do not build locally).**
   - Current main: `gh run download 43696254970 -R BbrSofiane/email-os -n email-os-android-fixture-debug -D <dir>` (push run on `3061e54`).
   - Pre-unification (for the reset test): the same artifact name from run `43645874365` (PR #63, head `63f7ab8`).
   - Record the SHA-256 of each APK you install.
3. **Protect what is on the emulator.** Package id is `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture`. If it is already installed, save its data directory first (`adb shell run-as … tar` to a tarball in your scratchpad) and tell me the path in your report. Then uninstall.
4. **Fresh-install smoke on the main APK.** Follow the steps in `docs/development.md` ("Android fixture APK") and at least cover what the previous smoke covered (see `docs/current-status.md`, "Android fixture target"): inbox renders, open a conversation, Mark done, restart the process and the conversation is still gone, Gmail controls and Files/links absent, save a draft and reopen it with exact subject and body, background/resume keeps the editor intact. Add what is new since unification: the seeded read/unread mix is visible (6 of 16 read), star and mark read/unread work, and Undo after Mark done restores the row.
5. **Legacy reset on a device.** Get a real legacy profile (one created by the pre-unification APK: archive something and save a draft in it), then run the main APK over it and check: the reset screen appears before any mailbox; closing the app at that screen changes nothing; accepting it leads to the mailbox with 16 Inbox rows; the saved draft is still there with its exact text; a second launch shows no reset screen. If `adb install -r` refuses because the two CI APKs are signed with different debug keys, carry the data across with `run-as` (tar the data dir out of the old install, uninstall, install main, restore, launch). Say in the report which route you used. If you can inspect the app's files with `run-as`, also confirm one backup file exists under `backups/` and `mail.db` is gone.
6. **Evidence.** Take screenshots at the key points with `device_screenshot` and refresh `docs/validation/android-smoke/` with the ones worth keeping (same naming style; a few, not dozens).
7. **PR.** Update `docs/current-status.md` (and `docs/development.md` only if a smoke step is wrong or missing) so it states what was run, on which APK hash and commit, and what was seen. Open a PR to `main` on `BbrSofiane/email-os` (the git remote is a proxy URL, so pass `-R BbrSofiane/email-os` to `gh`). Do not merge it.

## Rules
- Synthetic fixture data only. No real accounts, credentials or Google network.
- If something fails or looks wrong, that is the result I need: capture the screenshot and `adb logcat` excerpt, try once more to rule out a flake, and report it. Do not fix product code in this thread and do not word the docs around it.
- Write down only what you saw. Anything you could not check goes under a "Not verified" heading.
- Never touch the root checkout `/home/exedev/email-os` (the owner's work). Work in your own worktree.
- Do not run cargo or the Android build here; other threads are using the machine.

## Report
End with: pass or fail per step, APK hashes, which reset route you used, anything not verified, the path of any data backup you made, and the PR URL.

The main APK is freshly installed after I uninstalled the old one, which was blocked by a signature mismatch, once its data was backed up. The app is launching now, and I'm starting the fresh-install smoke test next.

items.text: My glob wasn't expanded on the device. I'll pull the file by exact name and inspect it.
Legacy draft survived with exact text. Last reset check: second launch.
Smoke done. Now the docs. I'll record what I saw, including the failures.

The smoke found four real problems on the main APK: a one-off ANR, an overlapping reader toolbar, Undo expiring, and a reset screen that doesn't fully match what it says. The rest passed. I opened PR #72 and did not merge it.

**PR:** https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/72

## Pass or fail per step
- **1. Device:** pass. `agent-device` drove the UI; `adb` was used for installs, `run-as` and logs only.
- **2. APKs:** pass. Both came from CI and nothing was built locally.
- **3. Protect existing data:** pass. The package was already installed (the old APK, with a 14 Nov profile), so I backed up its data before uninstalling.
- **4. Fresh-install smoke on main:** mostly pass, with findings.
  - **Passed:**
    - The inbox shows 16 rows, 6 read and 10 unread.
    - Mark done survives a process kill.
    - Mark read/unread works from the reader button and the row menu.
    - Star/Unstar works, but only from the command palette; there is no star in the row menu or reader toolbar.
    - Gmail controls and Files/links are absent.
    - A saved draft reopens with exact text, and the editor survives background/resume.
  - **Undo:** it restored the row when I tapped it within about 2 seconds of Mark done. A first attempt, tapped well after the toast, showed "Undo expired".
  - **ANR:** one ANR on the first cold launch (details below).
- **5. Legacy reset:** pass.
  - **Reset screen:** it appears before any mailbox.
  - **Cancel:** closing the app there left the legacy `mail.db` and drafts byte-identical, and the screen returned on the next launch.
  - **After accepting:** 16 inbox rows, the saved draft intact with exact text, one file in `backups/`, and `mail.db` gone.
  - **Second launch:** no reset screen.
  - **Backup:** it passes `PRAGMA integrity_check` and holds 18 conversations.
- **6. Evidence:** pass. Nine screenshots in `docs/validation/android-smoke/`; the two draft images replace the 14 Nov ones of the same name.
- **7. PR:** pass. `docs/current-status.md` has the full account and `docs/development.md` has two corrections.

## Failures and oddities, recorded as seen
- **ANR:** once on the first cold launch after install, logged as input dispatch timed out waiting for focus. The host was loaded (load average 4.1 on 4 cores). It did not recur on about six later cold launches. Screenshot: `first-launch-anr.png`.
- **Reader toolbar overlap:** the UI tree puts Close (Esc) at x 212–301 and Remind me at x 199–286, and the "Inbox" title is drawn over the icons. Tapping Close opened the reminder UI twice instead of closing the reader.
- **Mark done:** it leaves the reader open on a neighbouring conversation. It does not return to the inbox, so I corrected that step in `docs/development.md`.
- **Reset screen:**
  - **Files created early:** `gmail.db` and `synthetic-provider.db` are created while the reset screen is up, before accepting.
  - **Copy mismatch:** the copy says "18 sample conversations", but the inbox shows 16.
- **Cosmetic:** the Drafts list row truncates the subject to "Ar", and every inbox row says "Has attachments", including the Invoice row whose preview says there are none.
